rules.title: Rent Control and Rent Increase Procedures
rules.requirement: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents. Municipalities may pass ordinances establishing rent control or rent leveling. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years following completion. A landlord cannot raise rent mid-lease; the old lease must be terminated and a new lease with increased rent offered with proper written notice. Rent increases must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal ordinances.
rules.summary_plain: In New Jersey, rent control is set by cities, not the state. Landlords cannot raise rent during a lease but can increase rent when offering a new lease with proper notice. Rent increases must be reasonable and follow local rules.
rules.summary_plain_es: En Nueva Jersey, el control de alquileres lo establecen las ciudades, no el estado. Los propietarios no pueden aumentar el alquiler durante un contrato, pero pueden aumentar el alquiler al ofrecer un nuevo contrato con el aviso adecuado. Los aumentos deben ser razonables y seguir las reglas locales.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies statewide except where local rent control ordinances exist; newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt for 30 years after construction.

conditions.note: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt for 30 years after completion

rules.exemptions_text: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years; government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.
rules.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents. Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling. ... Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building. ... A landlord cannot raise the rent mid-lease term. The old lease must be terminated, and the new lease must have the increased rental payment. The landlord has to offer the tenant a new lease with the increased rent once the old lease has been terminated. ... Notice requirements for rent increases are contained in the Anti -Eviction Act ( N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 et seq.). This law provides that before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent. The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
